result.note: Tested the RBI's regulatory measures against rupee speculation; skipped market levels, bank stock moves and the Jefferies loss estimate.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the measures taken by the Reserve Bank of India between 30 March and 1 April 2026 to curb speculation against the rupee:
items: The RBI capped banks' net open rupee positions at USD 100 million.
The RBI banned rupee non-deliverable forwards.
The RBI allowed companies to rebook cancelled forward contracts to ease hedging.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the RBI barred companies from rebooking cancelled forward contracts. It added this curb, together with the ban on rupee non-deliverable forwards, after banks responded to the USD 100 million cap on net open positions by offloading positions to corporates and hedge funds. The rupee then surged 1.8% to 93.10 per dollar on 2 April 2026, its best session since 2013.
questions.source: the central bank followed up on Wednesday by banning rupee non-deliverable forwards and barring companies from rebooking cancelled forward contracts.
